claims.summary: A manifest lists an image’s layers and configuration. — The frozen storage unit says a manifest lists an artifact’s layers and configuration. This directly supplies the individual image’s internal component description requested by the stem.

A repository groups differently tagged images under one image name. — The frozen unit describes a repository as a collection of same-name images with different tags. This literal statement is correct for explaining image-family organization, but it does not describe one image’s components or sharing of stored layer content.

Images can share identical content-addressed layers. — The frozen unit describes content-addressable layers and sharing identical common layers across images. This directly addresses storage reuse, the second requested representation topic.

A tag supplies a human-readable reference that can move to another image. — The frozen unit documents human-readable mutable tags that can move to a new image. This literal statement is appropriate when explaining reference naming or update-following aliases; it does not explain internal image composition or shared layer storage.

Treat useful reader concurrency as capped at four for this consumer group. — The Event Hubs section of the frozen KEDA unit permits one reader per partition within a consumer group and identifies partitions as the useful replica bound. All four partitions already have assigned readers, so the useful simultaneous-reader ceiling remains four under the stated topology.

Raise maxReplicas from four to twelve to allow more replicas. — maxReplicas is a real replica limit. Raising it is appropriate when the cap blocks demanded replicas and sufficient unassigned partitions are available. Allowing more replicas cannot add useful partition readers when every partition in this fixed group already has a reader.

Lower unprocessedEventThreshold to request replicas at a smaller lag. — The frozen KEDA unit identifies unprocessedEventThreshold as the lag threshold used to request Event Hubs scaling. Lowering it is an appropriate demand adjustment when threshold-delayed scale-out, available replica headroom and unassigned partitions permit additional useful readers. It does not create partitions or add reader assignments beyond the four already occupied here.

Retain the selector, change the Service port and check DNS again. — A Service port change is appropriate for a confirmed forwarding mismatch when selector membership is correct. Here the ports already match and the selector chooses no Pods in ai-workloads, so a port change and another DNS check cannot establish backing membership.

Set the Service selector to app=text-api, inspect EndpointSlices and send a request through the Service. — The frozen Service and troubleshooting units connect Service selectors to matching Pod labels, and the connectivity unit verifies EndpointSlice addresses plus requests in the target namespace. Service and intended Ready Pods are now explicitly in ai-workloads, so correcting the selector addresses the stated membership defect without changing the Deployment labels.

Change the Deployment Pod labels to app=text-service and replace the Pods. — Changing the Deployment’s Pod template labels is a documented alternative when the Service and Pods share a namespace and changing those labels is permitted. The shared namespace now holds, but this stem explicitly requires Deployment labels to remain unchanged.
